# engineering/rendering/fabric-shading

<!-- Generated by scripts/okf.py index. Do not edit by hand. -->

# Section

* [Fabric shading](about.md) - How each leotard fabric family is shaded in real time: a GGX base plus optional sheen, anisotropy, coat, thin-film, diffraction and coverage layers, the custom techniques (foil dots, diffraction, velvet pile, mesh over skin, stretch, neon), starting values and calibration.

# Technique

* [Calibrating fabric materials against physical swatches](calibration-against-swatches.md) - Because no optical data exists for leotard fabrics, tune each preset by eye or optimisation against photographs and video of real swatches: flatbed scan, multi-light photos, backlit shots, shots at known stretch, a moving-light cylinder video and a colour target in every shot.
* [Foil-dot (mystique) mixing](foil-dot-mixing.md) - Shade mystique as a pattern-space dot mask that mixes a metal foil BRDF with the dyed-fabric BRDF; when dots shrink below a pixel, sum both lobes by coverage rather than averaging their parameters, and lower coverage under stretch.
* [Holographic foil diffraction](holographic-diffraction.md) - Hologram foil is a spatially varying 1D diffraction grating; shade it as a foil lobe plus a first-order grating term (Stam 2004) driven by per-texel groove orientation and period, with a multi-tap environment approximation; hue-ramp tricks are a low-end fallback.
* [Mesh over skin in one shader](mesh-over-skin-blend.md) - Because a leotard is skin-tight, shade sheer mesh by compositing it over the skin or lining at the same point inside one shader, with view-angle-dependent coverage, instead of using sorted transparency; alpha-to-coverage or OIT are the fallbacks.
* [Neon and fluorescent fabric colours](neon-colours.md) (draft) - Fluorescent leotard colours are physically brighter than any reflectance-only RGB albedo allows; emulate with a lighting-responsive fluorescence gain, a wide-gamut working space and Display P3 output, under a colour-preserving tone mapper (Khronos PBR Neutral).
* [Per-fabric shading recipe](per-fabric-shading-recipe.md) - One forward-shaded material built from a GGX base plus optional layers (sheen/fuzz, anisotropy, clear coat, thin film, diffraction, coverage) renders every leotard fabric family; which layers each family needs, which ship in three.js and which are custom.
* [Starting parameter values per fabric (guesses)](starting-parameter-values.md) (draft) - Proposed roughness, anisotropy, sheen, coat, foil, thin-film and fuzz starting values per fabric family from the shading research, beside the values the proof of concept actually uses; all are unmeasured guesses to be tuned against swatches.
* [Stretch-dependent fabric appearance (open problem)](stretch-dependent-appearance.md) (draft) - Stretched knit lightens, shows the skin or lining, loses foil coverage and printed colour; there is no rendering literature or format support for this, so the proposal is an in-house model driven by per-triangle strain and fitted to swatches photographed at known stretch.
* [Importing scanned fabric textures (VMOD and PBR map sets)](texture-import-pipeline.md) (draft) - How downloaded fabric materials (the owner's proposed source is VMOD by SwatchOn) enter the app: PNG/TIFF PBR map sets with a stated real-world size, converted to compressed GPU textures and applied in per-panel cloth-space UVs, with textures supplying structure and the existing shader layers supplying sparkle, foil flash, hologram and mesh-over-skin; plus the licence caveat.
* [Velvet pile shading](velvet-pile.md) - Shade velvet with a dominant sheen/fuzz lobe over a dark base, tilt that lobe by a per-panel nap direction so the fabric reads lighter or darker with the pile, drive the direction with a flow map for crushed velvet, and reserve shell rendering for close-ups.
